### Summary

At the pin two numerics switches remain environment variables: `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` (XC, @sec-ch12-centroid) and
`SNAP_ANOMALY`, which overrides the deck key `dynamics/anomaly` (anomaly storage, the precision chapter's subject).
The other numerics selectors are deck keys: `dynamics/conversion-order`, `dynamics/flux-covariance` and
`dynamics/x1-mass-covariance` (@sec-ch12-wb-reference, @sec-ch12-flux-covariance, @sec-ch12-mass-covariance). The
corrected face work has no switch at all (@sec-ch12-radial-exact). The two variables are parsed differently:

- XC is read once per process and cached, so a comparison needs one child process per arm.
- `SNAP_ANOMALY` is read each time a deck is parsed, and a value it does not know is refused.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Parses the two process-environment numerics switches.

**Data.** Environment strings in; a cached boolean (XC) or an overridden deck option (`SNAP_ANOMALY`) out.

**Placement.** XC at its first accessor call, which can be during setup; `SNAP_ANOMALY` when the hydro options are
read from a deck.

**Activation.** XC off by default; `SNAP_ANOMALY` unset leaves the deck's `anomaly` key in force.

**Guarantee / limits.** XC has no spelling validation and no cross-rank agreement check; `SNAP_ANOMALY` refuses a
value outside its word lists.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-environment-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

| value | XC (`x1_centroid_exact_enabled`) | `SNAP_ANOMALY` |
|---|---|---|
| unset | off | the deck's `anomaly` key |
| empty string | off | off |
| `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` | off (compared after lower-casing) | off (compared as written) |
| `1`, `true`, `on`, `yes` | on | on |
| every other string | on | refused: "must be 0 or 1" |

: The parse of the two environment switches at the pin. {#tbl-ch12-environment-parse}

XC does no trimming: `false ` with a trailing space is "every other string" and turns it on. Every block in one
process sees the same cached XC value. The code does not by itself make different MPI[^rg-16de4a84d046] processes agree.

### Derivation

No numerical equation is added. `get_env` ({{< code src/layout/layout.hpp get_env >}}) returns the environment string
when the variable is set, and otherwise the default the caller passes. `x1_centroid_exact_enabled`
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}) passes the default `"0"`, lower-cases the string,
compares it with the empty string, `0`, `false`, `off` and `no`, and stores the result in a function-local static.
`SNAP_ANOMALY` is the `env` field of the `anomaly` row of the options schema
({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}}). The reader that `tools/gen_options.py` generates from it applies the
override after it reads the deck. It sets true for `1`, `on`, `true` and `yes`, sets false for the empty string,
`0`, `off`, `false` and `no`, and refuses anything else, with no lower-casing (`TRUE_WORDS`, `FALSE_WORDS` and
`env` in {{< code tools/gen_options.py env >}}). The hydro options reader calls it
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).

The off-by-default rows of `[C1]` match XC's parser. `[C1]`'s other rows and its implication model switches that the
code at the pin does not read, and no claim here rests on them [check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

For XC, launch child A with its environment, let its first accessor call fix the flag, and run all its blocks with
that cached value. Then launch child B separately for the other arm. The first call can come during setup, before a
time step, so changing XC between RK stages is not a valid experiment. A test that inherits the user's environment
can run a nominal default arm with XC set by the shell. `test_x1_centroid_rest_python` therefore pops the variable
from its children's environment before it sets the arm ({{< code tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py run >}}).

### Code

**How to use it.** Start a fresh process for each XC arm, and set it on every rank before importing or
constructing the solver. Use the CTest registration to obtain an arm's environment (@sec-ch12-matrix):

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -R '^test_x1_seam_split_x1_centroid' --output-on-failure
```

Run this command from the checkout root after configuring the import path (@sec-ch12-test-environment).
Set `dynamics/conversion-order`, `flux-covariance` and `x1-mass-covariance` in the deck. They are not read from the
environment.

`x1_centroid_exact_enabled` ({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}) contains this
selection step:

```cpp
    auto v = get_env("SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT", "0");
    std::transform(v.begin(), v.end(), v.begin(),
                   [](unsigned char c) { return std::tolower(c); });
    return !(v.empty() || v == "0" || v == "false" || v == "off" || v == "no");
```

The enclosing lambda initializes a function-local `static const bool`, so changing the environment afterwards has no
effect.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| env | {{< code src/layout/layout.hpp get_env >}} | `get_env` | `SNAP_*` |
| xc | {{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}} | `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` | `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` |
| anomaly row | {{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}} | `env: SNAP_ANOMALY` | `SNAP_ANOMALY` |
| override | {{< code tools/gen_options.py env >}} | `env` | `SNAP_ANOMALY` |
| xc arms | {{< code tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py run >}} | `run` | `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` |
| anomaly arm | {{< code tests/test_anomaly_storage.py arm_switch >}} | `arm_switch` | `SNAP_ANOMALY` |

: Implementation sites for the environment switches. {#tbl-ch12-environment-code}

1. Read the string, or the default `"0"` when XC is absent, and cache the boolean. The anchor
   `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` is in {{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}.
2. For `SNAP_ANOMALY`, read the deck first, then apply the override, refusing an unknown word. The anchor `env` is in
   {{< code tools/gen_options.py env >}}.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_x1_centroid_rest_python` | the unset arm and the `1` arm, each in a child process with the variable popped first | `TOL_ON`, `TOL_OFF` | the script |
| `test_x1_seam_split.<b>` (`switches_off_nghost_1_sets_up`) | the default arm asserts that XC is unset | exact | the test |
| `test_anomaly_storage_python` (`switch` arm) | `SNAP_ANOMALY=1` in a child turns anomaly storage on without the YAML key; an unsupported EOS[^rg-fe974e22df0a] refuses it | string match | the script |
| `configuration_check.py` `[C1]` (report check) | the off-by-default parser rows | exact symbolic or Boolean equality | the independent check |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-environment-tests}

The XC arms are set in `run` ({{< code tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py run >}}). The default arm's assertion is in
{{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.switches_off_nghost_1_sets_up >}}. The `SNAP_ANOMALY` arm is
`arm_switch` ({{< code tests/test_anomaly_storage.py arm_switch >}}).

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch16-ch12-tests.

The independent report check verifies the parser truth table in `[C1]`.[^ch12-environment-run] It models a
contract and does not execute the compiled solver. Only its off-by-default rows describe a parser at the pin.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The independent parser check does not execute the C++ static storage. Cross-rank consistency of XC is a launch
responsibility. Any XC string outside the false tokens silently turns it on. `SNAP_ANOMALY` is case-sensitive:
`TRUE` is refused, not read as on.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
